sections.h2: What the Mecklenburg County Register of Deeds does
sections.html:
This is the county's public archive for land and business filings. Staff accept documents for registration, index them and store them, so anyone can trace who owns a Charlotte lot or a Davidson farmhouse.

On the real estate side the office handles conveyances, deeds of trust, mortgages, powers of attorney, assumed business names, separation agreements and plats. The same counter issues marriage licenses, swears in notaries, records military discharge papers and holds vital records.

The office website posts holiday closings, so check it before planning a trip downtown.

Two databases cover the full span. The modern one holds real estate documents from March 1990 to the present. The historic one holds land records and images from 1763 through February 1990. Physical records can also be inspected at the office from half past eight to half past four.

Title work on an old parcel often crosses the 1990 line: a recent deed of trust sits in the modern index, while the older chain of conveyances sits in the historic one. If you inherited the house, search under the family name and the previous owner's name to see what is still of record, such as a mortgage that was never released.

Registration decides who stands first. G.S. 47-18 provides that a conveyance does not defeat lien creditors or paying purchasers until it is registered where the land lies, and rank follows the order of filing.

In practice, a creditor's claim could still beat your buyer until the new deed is indexed. Ask your closing attorney when the package will be submitted, and whether the buyer's deed of trust is going in right behind your deed. Keep the recording confirmation after closing. If a question about the date ever comes up, that proof settles it.

Mecklenburg posts a Uniform Fee Schedule that follows G.S. 161-10. The amounts sellers meet most often are below, and every added page beyond the allowance costs $4.

Fees most often paid on a Mecklenburg sale
ServicePosted amount
Deed and other general instruments$26 for 15 pages
Loan security instrument$64 for 35 pages
Document outside format rules$25 extra
Mortgage satisfactionFree

Other charges: a certified copy is $5 for page one and $2 for the rest. Plain copies are 25 cents a page at the counter or $1 by mail. A plat is $21 a sheet, and each extra instrument in one filing is $10. Party names past twenty cost $2 each in index fees.

G.S. 161-14(b) sets the layout. A document that misses it is still accepted, for the $25 surcharge. The county's checklist has five points.

  • Paper: 8.5 inches wide, 11 or 14 inches tall.
  • Margins: three open inches above the text on sheet one, a quarter inch elsewhere.
  • Type: black on white, nine points or larger. Pen is allowed for blanks and corrections.
  • Sides: print on one side only.
  • Heading: a label naming the kind of instrument on the first sheet.

If you drafted a document yourself, run it against this list before you submit it.

sections.h2: The deed tax and who covers it
sections.html:
Sellers carry this cost. G.S. 105-228.30 sets one dollar for each $500 of price, with part of a $500 block rounded up, and the office collects it before it records the deed.

The county keeps half and the state receives the other half. Your settlement statement shows the dollar figure for your sale price.

sections.h2: What to check in the records before listing
sections.html:
Three places answer three different questions. The Register of Deeds shows what is recorded against the parcel. The county's property record card shows how Tax Administration describes the house. The Tax Collector shows what is owed.

  • Recorded deeds of trust with no matching satisfaction. A loan you paid off can still look open if the lender never filed its release.
  • The name on the latest deed. On an inherited property, the last recorded owner is often the person who died.
  • The property record card at Reval.MeckNC.gov, which lists bedrooms, bathrooms and other features the county uses to value the house.
  • The county's no-cost alert service, so a later filing under your name reaches you.

A closing attorney will run a full title search regardless. A light version first tells you whether the sale will be quick or whether an old lien, a missing release or an unprobated estate needs to be cleared up.

sections.h2: From signed deed to public record
sections.html:
Four steps carry a deed from signature to the index. The state treats its fee list as complete and exclusive, so payment is due when you file.

  • Match the grantor's name and legal description to the prior deed.
  • Have the seller's side cover the excise tax.
  • Add the page-count fee and any surcharge.
  • Hand in the original and keep proof that it was recorded.

A lender's satisfaction after payoff is recorded free and shows up in the index afterward.

sections.h2: Disabled veteran relief and other offices
sections.html:
Military discharge papers are recorded at this office. A property tax break for a disabled veteran is a separate matter: the applicant completes Form NCDVA-9 with a veteran service officer and files with the county assessor. The exclusion covers $45,000 of value and has no age or income cutoff.

The register is an elected county officer, chosen every two years under G.S. 161-1. Questions about deed wording or title for a specific house belong with a closing attorney. Value and exemption questions go to Tax Administration.

For context on the market you are selling into: 1,233,383 residents in mid 2025, a median owner value of $406,800 for 2020 to 2024, and 55.1 percent of homes owner-occupied.

sections.h2: Paying at the counter and guarding your title
sections.html:
The counter takes cash, Mastercard, Visa and Discover, checks, money orders and approved escrow accounts. A check needs a printed name and address and a phone number, made out to the Mecklenburg County Register of Deeds. Starter and counter checks are turned away, and a bounced check may cost $35.

The office runs a no-cost Property Fraud Alert that notifies you when any document under your name reaches the records, which suits owners of vacant or inherited houses. Anyone buying on a contract for deed should know that Chapter 47H obliges the seller to record the contract, or a memorandum of it, within five business days.

If you own a Mecklenburg house burdened by back taxes, a title snag or a difficult tenant, a cash buyer can set a closing date that works, with a closing attorney handling the recording.

faqs.q: What does Mecklenburg County charge to file a deed?
faqs.a: $26 covers the first fifteen pages, plus $4 for each page past that. A loan instrument costs $64 for thirty-five pages. Documents outside the format rules carry a $25 surcharge.

faqs.q: Which party pays the deed stamp tax in a Mecklenburg sale?
faqs.a: The seller owes it. The rate is one dollar per $500 of price, rounded up for a partial block, and it is due at the counter.

faqs.q: Does recording a mortgage satisfaction cost anything?
faqs.a: No. The fee schedule lists satisfaction instruments as free, so your only task is confirming that your lender files one after payoff.

faqs.q: Can I look up Mecklenburg land records on my own?
faqs.a: Yes. A modern online database covers documents from March 1990 forward, a historic index covers 1763 through February 1990, and records can be inspected at the office from half past eight to half past four.

faqs.q: What happens to a deed that breaks the format rules?
faqs.a: It is still recorded, but you pay $25 on top of the usual fees. Margins, tiny type and two-sided pages cause most of those cases.
